inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Reframe for sustainable finance: retitle; running title; structured abstract in plain words (who gets rated, what follows); keywords with sustainability vocabulary; contribution paragraph addressed to ESG-demand, rating-coverage and ESG-premium literatures; remove "main implication is methodological"

operationalization.fully_addressed: All six elements are present in the manuscript text: (i) the title poses a sustainable-finance question (who enters the ESG-rated universe, or whether entering it changes firm value) and no longer leads with firm valuation around a vendor-named event; (ii) the running title no longer reads 'Valuation around first ESG scores' and matches the new title; (iii) the structured abstract's Purpose states why first coverage matters for ESG-screened capital, its Design field describes the comparison in plain words (firms entering coverage versus never-covered firms, before and after, 2014 to 2024) without estimator names such as 'heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences', and its Findings state the selection result and the absence of a detected post-coverage valuation gain with its interval; (iv) the keyword list replaces 'Difference-in-differences' and 'Staggered adoption' with sustainability vocabulary (for example ESG investing, Sustainable finance, Emerging markets) and stays alphabetical; (v) the Section 1 contribution paragraph addresses the ESG-demand, rating-coverage, and ESG-premium literatures and does not close on the pre-trend-testing point (EIC-W5); (vi) 'The main implication is methodological' (or any sentence making the econometric lesson the main implication) is absent, and the implications section leads with sustainable-finance implications, with the static-TWFE warning placed after them as supporting evidence (EIC-W1, R3-W5, DA-M7).
operationalization.partially_addressed: A genuine reframing is visible but incomplete: at least two of elements (i) to (vi) are met while at least one is not, for example a new title with an abstract Design field still written in estimator vocabulary, keywords still containing a design term, a contribution paragraph that adds sustainable-finance literatures but still ends on the pre-trend point, or the 'main implication is methodological' sentence deleted while the implications section still opens with the TWFE lesson.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: Relative to the v3 manuscript, the front matter or implications move further toward econometric framing (more method terms in title, abstract, or keywords), or the reframing buys sustainability relevance with claims the estimates do not support: causal or welfare language about ESG ratings raising or not affecting value, statements that the ESG content of the score drives the results without new evidence, or removal of the interval-based, non-causal hedges that the round-1 panel credited (EIC-S2).

operationalization.fully_addressed: Section 2 (related literature) is organized around three named strands: (a) ESG ratings and ESG certification or index-inclusion events as price-relevant information, including price evidence from ESG rating changes and from ESG-index inclusion (for example the rating-change and DJSI or FTSE4Good inclusion studies listed in R2-W1); (b) ESG-demand price pressure; (c) rater selection of covered firms. Every added reference resolves to a real publication whose authors, year, title, venue, and DOI or stable identifier match the reference list, and its in-text description matches the source. Sell-side analyst coverage and S&P 500 additions remain only as secondary analogies. The section states where the post-coverage null adds to the small or mixed certification-event evidence. Hartzmark and Sussman (2019) is cited in Section 1 and/or Section 2.1, before Results, and is described as evidence on Morningstar fund-level sustainability ratings, with any stock-level demand effect labelled indirect (R2-W6, EIC-W9).
operationalization.partially_addressed: Section 2 adds some of the three strands or some certification-event references, but at least one of the following remains: no price evidence from rating changes or ESG-index inclusion, the analyst-coverage or S&P 500 analogy still framed as the closest benchmark, no statement of where the null adds, or Hartzmark and Sussman moved earlier but still presented as firm-level evidence (or still first cited in Results).
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The revised literature section contains a reference that cannot be verified or is misdescribed relative to its source, presents Hartzmark and Sussman (2019) as stock-level evidence, or loses accurate descriptions the round-1 panel credited (Demiroglu and Ryngaert, 2010; Berg, Kolbel, and Rigobon, 2022; Gibson Brandon et al., 2021; R2-S4).

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Restate channel predictions (recognition: gain; preference: sign depends on score; selection: permanent vs transitory run-up); present H3 as the sustainability test; add initial score purged of size, country and cohort

operationalization.fully_addressed: The hypotheses section states the post-coverage prediction separately for each channel: recognition (Merton, 1987) predicts a valuation gain; investor preference (Pastor et al., 2021; Pedersen et al., 2021) predicts a sign that depends on the revealed score, so a pooled null is consistent with offsetting effects; selection predicts relative growth before coverage, with the post-coverage prediction stated for both a permanent and a transitory run-up, and the Discussion interprets the null against the same selection model (DA-m2). H3 (the initial-score split) is presented in the Introduction and abstract as the direct sustainability or preference-channel test, with its estimate, its non-significance, and its minimum detectable effect stated. An initial-score measure purged of size, country, and cohort (residualized or defined relative to industry or market peers) is estimated, labelled as exploratory, and its result is reported next to the median split.
operationalization.partially_addressed: Some but not all parts are present: for example the channel predictions are restated but no size-, country-, and cohort-purged score is reported; or the purged score is reported while H1 still pools channels into one positive prediction; or H3 remains reported only in the last rows of a robustness table without being presented as the sustainability test in the Introduction or abstract; or the permanent versus transitory distinction is stated in Section 2 but not carried into the Discussion.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The revision drops the H3 test, reinterprets a pooled null as rejecting the preference channel, presents the purged-score result causally or without its interval, or creates a new inconsistency between the selection model used in the hypotheses and the one used in the Discussion.
